raw_segments.text: Shepherd, Fi, Daughter When my old wife lived, upon this day she
was both pantler, butler, cook, both dame and servant, welcome doll, serve doll, would
sing her song and dance her turn, now here at upper end a T.H. table, now I.T.H. middle,
on his shoulder and his, her face o' fire with labor, and the thing she took to quench
it she would to each one sip.
You are retired, as if you were a feasted one and not the hostess of the meeting.
Pray you, bid these unknown friends to swellcome, for it is a way to make us better friends
Come, quench your blushes and present yourself that which you are, mistress O.T.H. feast.
Come on and bid us welcome to your sheep shearing as your good flock shall prosper.
